source_snapshot.title: UAE traffic regulations 2027: Rules truck, bus and school bus drivers must follow
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Truck drivers and buses in the UAE will have a new set of driving regulations to follow from next year as the UAE is set to implement Cabinet Decision No. 174 of 2026 from January 1, 2027. The Decision covers various aspects that affect heavy goods vehicles and buses, however, not all the rules stipulated for truck and bus drivers may be entirely new. Zeiad Yehia, Legal Director at Al-Mur Law Firm, said: “Cabinet Decision No. 174 of 2026 ...introduces a comprehensive new executive regulatory framework for road traffic in the UAE. “The Resolution comprises 131 articles and comes into force on January 1, 2027. It implements Federal Decree-Law No. 14 of 2024 on the Regulation of Traffic, which itself came into force on March 29, 2025." Zeiad Yehia, Legal Director at Al-Mur Law Firm So, what does the new legislation say about the responsibilities of truck and bus drivers? Here’s all you need to know. Stopping in residential areas As per Article 17 (6), heavy vehicles or vehicles carrying heavy machinery and equipment must not stop in residential areas , unless they are parked for construction or development purposes. The law also requires the licensing and traffic authorities within each emirate to specify any roads, routes and timings during which heavy goods vehicles are prohibited from travelling. Overtaking rules Article 34 of the law also specifies that heavy buses and heavy goods vehicles should not overtake one another within city limits or near city borders, unless doing so does not obstruct traffic flow on the road. Also, in cases where there are designated lanes for heavy vehicles, drivers must not deviate from them. Six obligations of truck drivers Drivers of heavy goods vehicles should also follow these six rules at all times: 1. Stay on the right-most lane and not leave it unless necessary or when overtaking. 2. Ensure that the load on the truck does not exceed the load limit set by the licensing authority or the permitted height of the load. 3. Drivers cannot carry any passengers in heavy goods vehicles, except for the vehicle owner’s employees and loading and unloading staff, provided there are seats designated for them. 4. The vehicle’s load should not pose a danger to the public or obstruct traffic. 5. A cover must be fitted to prevent dust and other articles, such as sand, from leaking or being blown away from the truck load. 6. The load must not protrude beyond the vehicle’s dimensions in any way. Payload rules Article 37 of the Resolution also requires the driver to ensure that the payload is organised and arranged in a way that it is secure and fastened to the vehicle at all times and does not pose any danger to people or property. The load must also not obstruct the driver’s view, or obscure any hand signals, light signals, direction indicators, vehicle lights, mirrors or number plates. Passenger transport buses Article 33 of the Resolution also requires buses to have prominent signage indicating that it is authorised to carry paying passengers and the number of passengers permitted on the bus. Owners of the buses should also display a copy of the approved fare schedule in prominent places inside the bus or carry it on the bus so that it can be shown on request. Responsibilities of bus drivers Bus drivers must also ensure the following: The number of passengers does not exceed the limit authorised on the bus licence. Passengers must not stick their heads, hands or any part of their bodies out of the windows. The interior of the bus must be lit between sunset and sunrise, and whenever necessary. They do not stop to pick up or drop off passengers except at authorised locations. They do not speak to passengers while the bus is moving and not allow passengers to stand or sit next to them. They not refuse to carry any person who is willing to pay the prescribed fare, provided that the bus is not full. To inspect the vehicle right after the end of each journey, check for any items that may have been left behind and hand them over to the nearest police station within 24 hours. The police station must provide proof of this handover of item. School bus drivers When picking up and dropping off school pupils, drivers must ensure the following: They must park the vehicle parallel to the kerb in areas where it is permitted. Switch on the front and rear indicators. Open the side ‘stop’ indicator arm. Motorists must ensure that they come to a complete stop when they see a school bus stopped in such a manner. For two-way roads, vehicles in both directions must come to a complete stop and for roads that have a divider, vehicles in the same direction as a bus must come to a complete stop.

claims.claim: From January 1, 2027, UAE Cabinet Decision No. 174 of 2026 regulating heavy trucks and buses will come into force.
Truck drivers are prohibited from stopping in residential areas except for construction purposes.
Truck and bus drivers must follow special overtaking rules and use designated lanes.
Truck drivers must follow six main rules including load limits and prohibition of carrying passengers except employees.
Buses must have visible signs indicating authorized passenger capacity.
Buses must follow safety rules when transporting schoolchildren.

summary_ru: 🚌 Новые правила для водителей грузовиков и автобусов в ОАЭ с 2027 года 📅 С 1 января 2027 года в ОАЭ вступит в силу Постановление Кабинета №174 от 2026 года, регулирующее движение тяжелых грузовиков и автобусов. Водителям запрещено останавливаться в жилых районах, кроме случаев строительства, и предписывается соблюдать специальные правила обгона и движения по выделенным полосам. 🎓 Водители грузовиков должны соблюдать шесть основных правил, включая ограничение по загрузке и запрет перевозки пассажиров, кроме сотрудников. Автобусы обязаны иметь видимые таблички с разрешенным количеством пассажиров и соблюдать правила безопасности при перевозке школьников.
